comparator.name: Mathematics
comparator.sourceNotes: Reconstructed from the current official UvA Mathematics pages and the linked 2026-2027 programme table. The published curriculum totals 60+60+60=180 EC. Year 1 contains a broad compulsory foundation in sets and numbers, linear algebra, single- and multivariable analysis, graph theory, sequences and series, programming, numerical mathematics, probability, group theory, logic, iteration and visualisation, plus two tutorials. Year 2 develops geometry, vector calculus, rings and fields, statistics, ordinary differential equations, simulation and modelling, topology, mathematics communication and 18 EC of mathematics electives. Year 3 contains a tutorial, reflection on mathematics, a 12-EC bachelor project and 42 EC of mathematics electives and free-choice space. The official themes page organises possible choices into twelve overlapping themes, but a theme is advisory rather than a formal route: students may fill the choice space with mathematics courses, courses outside Mathematics, a minor or study abroad. The formal choice components are therefore preserved generically rather than inventing a theme, minor or individual electives. The overview confirms the BSc Mathematics award, 180 EC, Dutch full-time delivery and RIO code 56980.
components: Published third-year mathematics-elective and free-choice space; no theme, minor, exchange or individual elective is invented.
Published second-year mathematics-elective space; no theme or individual elective is invented.
Independent mathematical research project completed under researcher supervision and reported in a bachelor thesis.

core: Calculus, rigorous mathematical analysis and proof
Linear algebra and abstract algebraic structures
Discrete mathematics, logic and mathematical reasoning
Probability theory, mathematical statistics and stochastic systems
Differential equations, iteration and mathematical modelling
Mathematical modelling of real systems and solving real-world problems with mathematics
Programming, numerical methods and mathematical software
Reflection, communication and mathematical research practice
Independent bachelor research project in mathematics
questions: How can mathematical models describe change in systems such as epidemics, traffic flows and climate?
How can mathematics reveal patterns in data and improve concrete planning or financial decisions?
How does mathematics contribute to artificial intelligence, secure communication and other future technologies?

trace: teaches structured and object-oriented programming in Python together with elements of discrete mathematics and computational problem solving, extending the UvA first-year programming-and-experimentation foundation

covers differentiation, integration techniques, complex numbers and differential equations, the single-variable calculus foundation for all later analysis and modelling; it is technique-oriented rather than proof-based
treats logic, discrete structures and patterns with applications to algorithm construction, supplying formal logical reasoning and the discrete-mathematics foundation
treats systems of linear equations, vector spaces, linear transformations, determinants, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, with applications to Fourier series, difference equations and Markov chains
extends calculus to several variables and to differential equations and complex-valued functions, the multivariable-calculus and differential-equations content of the core

develops numerical root finding, interpolation, numerical differentiation and integration and the numerical solution of ordinary differential equations, with explicit attention to accuracy, stability and sensitivity to input

analyses linear time-invariant systems through differential equations, convolution, state-space models, Fourier series and the Fourier, Laplace and Z-transforms, the Fourier-analysis and linear-dynamical-systems content of the core
provides a foundation in mathematical statistics: probability theory, discrete and continuous distributions, sampling, parameter estimation and simulation
introduces research design and descriptive and inferential statistics up to analysis of variance, the applied statistical inference that complements mathematical probability and estimation

develops multivariate statistical models, including linear and logistic regression, factor analysis, analysis of covariance and non-parametric tests, extending statistical inference to models with many variables
teaches the design and performance analysis of algorithms and data structures, applying discrete mathematics and mathematical reasoning about efficiency to computational problems

studies modern algebraic algorithms, fast and arbitrary-precision arithmetic and advanced optimisation methods, giving computational contact with algebraic structures; it complements but does not replace courses in abstract algebra

covers search, constraint satisfaction, convex optimisation and linear and non-linear programming with laboratory projects, the optimisation methods behind planning problems such as schedules and routes
treats planning and optimal behaviour in non-deterministic environments under uncertainty, partial observability and resource constraints, modelling decisions in systems with random outcomes

studies populations, communities and ecosystems and devotes two weeks to ecological modelling as a tool for understanding and predicting ecological systems, the population-dynamics setting of mathematical modelling
teaches how to study disease occurrence, risks and changes over time in populations, including pandemics, the empirical field to which models of infectious-disease spread are applied

analyses the risk of crossing critical thresholds in the behaviour of Earth-system processes through the planetary-boundaries framework, introducing threshold behaviour of a real dynamical system, and is the formal gateway to Earth System Science Tools
teaches system modelling of the interacting biosphere, hydrosphere, lithosphere and atmosphere to study past and future climates, applying dynamical modelling to a real physical system

examines the nature of knowledge and the theoretical methods philosophers use to support conclusions, including the relation of philosophy to physics and computer science, the philosophical reflection on scientific knowledge that the core's philosophy component addresses
develops the main ethical theories and applies them to practical questions, the ethics component of the core

studies forward and inverse kinematics and motion planning in configuration space, including the structure of that space, applying linear algebra and geometric reasoning to rigid motions; it is an application of geometry and not a substitute for geometry or topology courses

processes and analyses digital images with point operators, local and morphological filters, edge detection and the Hough transform, applying convolution and transform methods to image data such as remote-sensing imagery

introduces linear regression, classification, resampling, shrinkage and tree-based methods, the statistical-learning models through which probability and statistics contribute to artificial intelligence
develops data cleaning, manipulation and visualisation for tabular, spatial and text data in code and ends with an independent data-analysis project answering a research question
builds and trains neural networks from scratch and with TensorFlow, applying linear algebra and multivariable calculus in gradient-based learning for vision and text data
introduces relational database theory, SQL, normalisation and query processing, the data-management layer of data science

teaches OLS, GLS and instrumental-variables estimation, t, F and LM tests and Monte Carlo study of sampling distributions, applying statistical estimation and testing to data and requiring an empirical paper
examines fairness, bias, privacy, responsibility and accountability in AI and algorithmic decision systems, the ethical questions raised by analysing and acting on data
treats reinforcement-learning frameworks and algorithms and has students implement agents that learn optimal behaviour from sequential trial-and-error data
integrates and analyses geospatial satellite and drone data with GIS to explore and model changes in the Earth system, the data-analysis side of satellite-image applications
introduces supply and demand, game theory, consumer and firm theory and market structure, the economic theory on which mathematical economics builds

develops advanced microeconomic theory: decisions under uncertainty, imperfect competition and strategic behaviour, general equilibrium and market efficiency, the subject matter that mathematical economics formalises
analyses market failure, public goods, externalities and taxation with theoretical models and empirical evidence, applying welfare economics to the choice of optimal policy
analyses national income, growth, inflation, unemployment, business cycles and fiscal and monetary policy, the economy-wide dynamics to which economic models are applied

teaches accounting theory and the analysis of financial statements as tools for understanding how economic events affect firms and their financing, the finance application of the economics direction; it is not a financial-mathematics course

alternatives.label: Mathematics, modelling & computation
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum rests on UCR's full mathematics sequence (Mathematical Methods, Linear Algebra, Advanced Calculus, Logic & Discrete Mathematics, Probability & Statistics, Computational & Numerical Methods, Linear Systems) with three further statistics courses, and adds two strands: computation and optimisation (Introduction to Programming, Algorithms & Data Structures, Advanced Algorithms, Optimization Methods in AI, Decision-making in AI) and the modelling of real systems (ecology, epidemiology, Earth-system modelling, robotics and image processing), closed by philosophy and ethics. The label names mathematics together with these two strands. It deliberately does not claim to be a full mathematics degree: UCR has no proof-based analysis, abstract algebra, geometry or topology sequence, all compulsory parts of the UvA foundation.
alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response to UvA's Mathematics bachelor: the complete UCR mathematics sequence in calculus, linear algebra, discrete mathematics and logic, probability and statistics, numerical methods and linear dynamical systems, programmed in Python and carried into algorithms, optimisation and the modelling of real natural and physical systems, with philosophy and ethics of knowledge. It reproduces the pure-and-applied, modelling-oriented core as far as UCR allows and leaves UvA's proof-based analysis, abstract algebra, geometry and topology as honest gaps.
progression: Introduction to Programming and Logic & Discrete Mathematics open the programme in semester 1, followed by Mathematical Methods in semester 2, which is the formal prerequisite of every later DISMATH course and of Robotics. Linear Algebra and Probability & Statistics in semester 3 precede Computational & Numerical Methods, Linear Systems, Advanced Algorithms and Robotics in semester 4, so numerical, transform and configuration-space methods follow matrix methods. Algorithms & Data Structures in semester 3 precedes Advanced Algorithms in semester 4. Research Methods & Statistics (semester 2) precedes the multivariate Statistics & Experimental Methods (semester 3), and both precede Machine Learning (semester 5) together with Linear Algebra and Probability & Statistics. Advanced Calculus is offered only in the second semester of a year and requires Mathematical Methods; semester 4 is filled by four courses offered only then, so semester 6 is its earliest feasible placement. Sustainability Essentials I in semester 1 is the formal prerequisite of Earth System Science Tools in semester 6; Ecosystems Uncovered is taken early as an introductory ecology course whose modelling component needs no formal mathematics prerequisite. Optimization Methods in AI and Image Processing & Computer Vision are placed in semester 6, after linear algebra, numerical methods and Linear Systems. Every course is offered in its assigned term and every formal prerequisite falls in an earlier semester.

alternatives.label: Mathematics, statistics & data science
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum keeps the shared mathematics sequence and builds on it a statistics and data-science strand of eleven courses: Research Methods & Statistics, Statistics & Experimental Methods, Econometrics, Introduction to Data Science, Database Management Systems, Machine Learning, Neural Networks & Deep Learning, Reinforcement Learning, Image Processing & Computer Vision, Earth Observation and AI Ethics, with epidemiology as a data-rich application. Mathematics and the statistics/data strand are of comparable weight, so the label names both rather than presenting the programme as a data-science degree.
alternatives.concept: A mathematics programme organised around the target's interests in probability, uncertainty and data analysis and UvA's Patterns in Data theme: the shared calculus, linear-algebra, probability and numerical foundation is carried into statistical inference and multivariate modelling, econometric estimation, data management and machine learning, and applied to image, satellite and population-health data, with attention to the ethics of data and algorithms.
progression: Introduction to Programming and Introduction to Data Science open the programme, so data handling in code is learned before any modelling course. Mathematical Methods in semester 2 is the formal prerequisite of Linear Algebra and Probability & Statistics in semester 3 and of Neural Networks & Deep Learning in semester 4, so gradient-based learning follows calculus and matrix methods. Research Methods & Statistics in semester 2 is the formal prerequisite of Econometrics in semester 6 and precedes Statistics & Experimental Methods and Machine Learning in semester 5, which build on probability and inference from semesters 2 and 3. Database Management Systems in semester 2 precedes the larger data projects of later years. Sustainability Essentials I in semester 1 is the formal prerequisite of Earth Observation in semester 4. Reinforcement Learning in semester 6 follows Neural Networks & Deep Learning, whose networks its agents use. Advanced Calculus is offered only in the second semester of a year and semester 4 is filled by courses offered only then, so it is taken in semester 6. Every course is offered in its assigned term and every formal prerequisite falls in an earlier semester.
alternatives.distinctness: The closest match applies the mathematics core to the modelling of natural and physical systems and to algorithms and optimisation. This alternative instead follows the evidenced probability, uncertainty and data-analysis direction, organising the programme around learning from data. It therefore removes seven courses of the closest match — Ecosystems Uncovered, Earth System Science Tools, Robotics, Advanced Algorithms, Optimization Methods in AI, Decision-making in AI and Introduction to Western Philosophy — and adds seven that the data concept requires: Introduction to Data Science, Database Management Systems, Neural Networks & Deep Learning, Econometrics, Reinforcement Learning, Earth Observation and AI Ethics. Epidemiology and image processing change role from modelling applications to data applications. The two programmes share seventeen courses and each contains 52.5 EC the other lacks.
traceOverrides: introduces linear regression, classification, resampling, shrinkage, tree-based methods, support vector machines and clustering, the core statistical-learning methods of data science

extracts structure from image and video data with filters, edge and shape detection, segmentation and object recognition, the data-science treatment of image data such as remote-sensing and medical images
teaches how to study disease, risks and change over time in populations and to evaluate evidence critically, an applied setting for the statistical analysis of population-health data

introduces Earth-system processes and their critical thresholds through the planetary-boundaries framework, the substantive context of satellite observations, and is the formal gateway to Earth Observation

alternatives.label: Mathematics, optimisation & economics
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum keeps the shared mathematics and statistics sequence and adds an optimisation and decision strand (Optimization Methods in AI, Decision-making in AI, Reinforcement Learning, Algorithms & Data Structures, Advanced Algorithms) and an economics strand (Introduction to Economics, Microeconomics & Behavior, Public Economics, International Macroeconomics, Econometrics, Accounting & Corporate Finance). The label names both strands beside mathematics; it does not claim the pure-mathematics or financial-mathematics depth available through UvA's electives.
alternatives.concept: A mathematics programme organised around the target's direct interest in financial mathematics and UvA's financial-mathematics and applied-mathematics choices: the shared mathematical foundation is carried into linear and non-linear optimisation, algorithmic optimisation, sequential decision-making under uncertainty and econometric estimation, and applied to formal economic theory of individual, strategic and market behaviour, public policy, the macroeconomy and corporate finance.
progression: Introduction to Programming, Logic & Discrete Mathematics and Introduction to Economics open the programme; Introduction to Economics precedes every later economics course that builds on it. Mathematical Methods and Research Methods & Statistics in semester 2 are the formal prerequisites of the DISMATH courses and of all BENECON 200- and 300-level courses respectively. Optimization Methods in AI is placed in semester 2: it requires only Introduction to Programming, and it introduces search, constraint satisfaction and linear programming before the later optimisation courses; its projects are revisited after Linear Algebra (semester 3) in Advanced Algorithms (semester 4), Decision-making in AI (semester 5) and Reinforcement Learning (semester 6). Algorithms & Data Structures in semester 3 precedes Advanced Algorithms in semester 4. Public Economics (semester 4) and Microeconomics & Behavior (semester 6) follow Introduction to Economics; Econometrics in semester 6 follows Probability & Statistics and Statistics & Experimental Methods. Advanced Calculus is offered only in the second semester of a year and semester 4 is filled by courses offered only then, so it is taken in semester 6. Every course is offered in its assigned term and every formal prerequisite falls in an earlier semester.
alternatives.distinctness: The closest match applies the mathematics core to the modelling of natural and physical systems; this alternative follows the evidenced financial-mathematics direction and applies the same foundation to economic behaviour and policy. It removes seven courses of the closest match — Ecosystems Uncovered, Epidemiology & Public Health, Sustainability Essentials I, Earth System Science Tools, Robotics, Image Processing & Computer Vision and Machine Learning — and adds Introduction to Economics, Microeconomics & Behavior, Public Economics, International Macroeconomics, Econometrics, Accounting & Corporate Finance and Reinforcement Learning, sharing seventeen courses with it. Against the statistics and data-science alternative it shares fifteen courses: the data-management, neural-network, satellite, image and data-ethics courses are replaced by economic theory and by optimisation and algorithm courses. In each pair every programme contains at least 52.5 EC the other lacks.
traceOverrides: covers search, constraint satisfaction, convex optimisation and linear and non-linear programming with laboratory projects, the mathematical-optimisation methods of the operations-research courses in the optimisation path and of planning problems such as schedules and routes
treats planning and optimal behaviour under uncertainty, partial observability and resource constraints, the decision-making-under-uncertainty theme of operations research
studies modern algebraic algorithms and advanced solution methods for optimisation problems with emphasis on mathematical modelling, extending optimisation into algorithm design
treats reinforcement-learning frameworks and algorithms for learning optimal policies in sequential decision problems, a computational approach to dynamic optimisation under uncertainty
teaches OLS, GLS and instrumental-variables estimation and t, F and LM tests with Monte Carlo analysis and requires an empirical paper, the statistical estimation of economic relationships

selection.assessment: The closest match owns the programme's general mathematics interests: abstract problem-solving, pattern recognition, proof, connections among fields, pure and applied mathematics, logic, modelling and persistence with difficult problems. UCR can implement calculus, linear algebra, discrete mathematics, probability, numerical methods, linear systems and applied modelling, while proof-based analysis, abstract algebra, geometry and topology remain visible gaps. Three specific directions remain. Probability, uncertainty and data analysis are implemented by UCR statistics, econometrics, databases, machine learning and neural-network courses and form the second alternative. Financial mathematics is implemented as the nearest feasible optimisation-and-economics direction through optimisation, decision-making, algorithms, economic theory and econometrics and forms the third. Mathematics with Computer Science and Mathematics with Physics are both evidenced stable directions, but three alternatives have already been reached; the former also substantially overlaps the closest alternative's computational core, while the latter would substitute broad physics applications for missing mathematical depth. Production therefore stops at the maximum of three alternatives.

blocks: Both are the programme's opening single-variable calculus course on differentiation and integration. UvA's Analyse 1 places this in a proof-oriented mathematics foundation; Mathematical Methods is technique-oriented and also covers complex numbers and differential equations.
Both extend calculus to functions of several variables. Advanced Calculus also treats differential equations and complex-valued functions, but it is less proof-oriented than UvA's Analyse 2.
Both treat discrete structures and graphs. UCR's course combines graph concepts with formal logic and applications to algorithm construction.
Verzamelingen en Getallen establishes sets, number systems and proof-based reasoning. UCR has no dedicated foundations-and-proof course, so no counterpart is claimed.
Rijen en reeksen develops sequences, series and their convergence. UCR's calculus courses use series but do not provide this dedicated proof-oriented component, so no second counterpart is claimed.
Inleiding Meetkunde is a dedicated geometry course. UCR has no geometry course, so no counterpart is claimed.

Inleiding Logica is a separate formal-logic course. UCR Logic & Discrete Mathematics supplies the content but is already matched to graph theory in this one-to-one comparison, so no second counterpart is claimed.
Both are the dedicated linear-algebra course: systems of linear equations, vector spaces, linear transformations and eigenvalues.

Algebra 1: groepentheorie is the first abstract-algebra course. UCR has no abstract-algebra course; Advanced Algorithms treats algebraic algorithms computationally and is not claimed as a counterpart.
Algebra 2: ringen en lichamen continues abstract algebra. UCR has no counterpart.
The second-year mathematics tutorial integrates and communicates mathematical work. UCR has no dedicated mathematics tutorial, so no counterpart is claimed.
Onderwijs en communicatie is a mathematics-communication project. UCR has no dedicated mathematics-communication course, so no counterpart is claimed.
Topology studies topological spaces and continuity abstractly. UCR has no counterpart.
The 18-EC second-year mathematics-choice space is preserved without inventing an elective; no single UCR course is claimed as its counterpart.
Differential equations, iteration & modelling of real systems
Vectorcalculus is a distinct UvA foundation component. UCR Advanced Calculus has already been matched to Analyse 2, so no second counterpart is claimed.

Gewone differentiaalvergelijkingen develops ordinary differential equations. UCR's calculus and numerical courses cover differential equations, but each is matched elsewhere, so no second counterpart is claimed.

Itereren en Visualiseren studies iterative processes and mathematical visualisation. UCR's modelling and computation courses use related techniques but do not provide the same dedicated component, so no counterpart is claimed.
Both are the mathematical-probability course: probability theory and discrete and continuous distributions. UCR's course also covers sampling, estimation and simulation.

Both teach statistical inference, including estimation and hypothesis testing. UvA's Stochastiek 2 develops it mathematically; Research Methods & Statistics is an applied course paired with research design, so the row shares the subject and function but not the mathematical depth.

Simuleren en modelleren develops simulation and mathematical modelling. UCR offers several applied modelling contexts, but no single course is a direct mathematical-modelling counterpart, so no match is claimed.

Both teach programming in Python from scratch. UCR's course is a full course that also covers object-oriented programming and elements of discrete mathematics; UvA's course combines programming with mathematical experimentation.
Both are the dedicated numerical-methods course: numerical root finding, interpolation, differentiation, integration and differential equations, with attention to accuracy.
Tutoraat Wiskunde integrates mathematical problem-solving and study skills. UCR has no dedicated mathematics tutorial, so no counterpart is claimed.
Tutoraat Wiskunde 1.2 continues integrated mathematical problem-solving and study skills. UCR has no dedicated mathematics tutorial, so no counterpart is claimed.
Wiskundetutoraat 3 develops presentation and mathematical-writing practice. UCR has no dedicated advanced mathematics tutorial, so no counterpart is claimed.
Reflectie op Wiskunde provides reflection on the discipline and its place in study and work. UCR philosophy courses add relevant context but are not direct counterparts, so no match is claimed.
Personal development, open profiling space & research

The 42-EC third-year mathematics-elective and free-choice space may contain mathematics electives, a minor, outside courses or study abroad. It is preserved as open space and not matched to any UCR course.
The Bachelorproject is an individual 12-EC mathematical research project and thesis. No scheduled UCR course is a thesis; UCR's optional independent research is shown in this row.

notes.text: The UvA programme includes a more extensive compulsory sequence in proof-oriented analysis, abstract algebra, geometry, topology, vector calculus, differential equations, simulation and mathematical research, together with 60 EC of later mathematics electives and free choice and a 12-EC bachelor project. At UCR, students can study calculus, advanced calculus, linear algebra, logic and discrete mathematics, probability and statistics, numerical methods and linear systems, and apply them in modelling, data science or optimisation, but UCR does not offer the same depth or sequence in pure mathematics.
